description:
The Financial Assistance for Education scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India under the aegis of the Goa Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (GBOCWWB). 

This scheme was officially launched in the year 2018. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the children of registered construction workers. 

The scheme aims to support the education of these children from the primary level up to the higher education level. 

The financial assistance is intended to alleviate the financial burden on construction workers who may struggle to afford educational expenses. 

The scheme has set measurable targets to ensure that a significant number of children benefit from this initiative. 

The GBOCWWB aims to provide assistance to at least 1,000 children annually through this scheme. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme varies based on the level of education. 

For students in primary education, the assistance is set at ₹5,000 per annum. 

For students in secondary education, the assistance increases to ₹10,000 per annum. 

For those pursuing higher education, the assistance is capped at ₹15,000 per annum. 

The total financial assistance can therefore reach up to ₹30,000 for a child who progresses from primary to higher education. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are specifically defined to ensure that the intended beneficiaries are reached. 

Only children of registered construction workers are eligible for this financial assistance. 

The construction worker must be registered with the GBOCWWB to qualify for the scheme. 

There is no specific age limit mentioned for the children. 

However, the educational qualifications must align with the respective levels of assistance. 

For primary education, the child must be enrolled in a recognized school. 

For secondary education, the child must be enrolled in a recognized secondary school or equivalent institution. 

For higher education, the child must be enrolled in a recognized college or university. 

The income criteria for the construction worker is also a crucial aspect of the eligibility. 

The family income of the construction worker must not exceed ₹8,000 per month. 

This income limit is set to ensure that the assistance reaches those who are genuinely in need. 

The application process for the Financial Assistance for Education scheme is straightforward. 

The construction worker must first ensure that they are registered with the GBOCWWB. 

Once registered, the worker can apply for financial assistance for their child. 

The application form can be obtained from the official GBOCWWB website or their local office. 

The applicant must fill out the form with accurate details regarding their child’s education. 

Along with the application form, several documents are required. 

These documents include the child’s birth certificate for age verification. 

The applicant must also provide proof of the child’s enrollment in the respective educational institution. 

Additionally, the construction worker must submit their registration certificate with the GBOCWWB. 

Proof of income must also be provided to verify that it does not exceed the specified limit. 

Once the application is complete with all necessary documents, it should be submitted to the GBOCWWB office. 

The timeline for processing applications typically takes about 30 days from the date of submission. 

Disbursement of funds is generally conducted on a quarterly basis. 

This means that once approved, the financial assistance will be credited to the bank account of the construction worker every three months. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Goa Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. 

The GBOCWWB operates under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of Goa. 

For any inquiries or assistance, individuals can contact the GBOCWWB office directly. 

The contact details for the GBOCWWB are available on their official website. 

The scheme has seen a positive response since its inception. 

Many construction workers have reported that the financial assistance has significantly helped in managing their children's educational expenses. 

The government has allocated a budget of ₹5 crore for this scheme for the financial year 2023-2024. 

This allocation is expected to cover the financial assistance for approximately 1,000 children. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to uplift the socio-economic status of construction workers in Goa. 

The GBOCWWB also conducts awareness programs to inform workers about the benefits available under this scheme. 

These programs are aimed at ensuring that eligible workers are aware of their rights and the assistance they can avail. 

The Financial Assistance for Education scheme is a vital step towards promoting education among the children of construction workers. 

By providing financial support, the government aims to reduce dropout rates in schools among these children. 

The scheme also encourages parents to prioritize education for their children. 

In addition to financial assistance, the GBOCWWB has other welfare schemes aimed at the holistic development of construction workers. 

These include health insurance schemes and skill development programs. 

The GBOCWWB is committed to improving the living standards of construction workers and their families. 

The Financial Assistance for Education scheme is a testament to this commitment. 

Overall, the scheme plays a crucial role in ensuring that the children of construction workers receive the education they deserve. 

By facilitating access to education, the government aims to break the cycle of poverty among construction worker families. 

The initiative reflects the government’s focus on inclusive growth and social welfare. 

The scheme is expected to continue evolving to meet the needs of construction workers and their families. 

In conclusion, the Financial Assistance for Education scheme by the GBOCWWB is a significant welfare initiative. 

It provides essential financial support to the children of registered construction workers. 

This support is crucial for promoting education and improving the socio-economic conditions of these families. 

The scheme is a vital part of the government’s broader efforts to uplift marginalized communities in India.
